rationale: The assistant followed a sensible path: seating/coupler first, told the customer to unplug before inspecting, and correctly identified the cracked, rounded-out drive coupler as the cause, then asked for the model before naming a part. It used only what the customer said and did not claim compatibility it could not confirm. The weak ending is the escalation: for a cheap clip-on coupler on a Sharp R272WM, telling the homeowner to get 'a local appliance repair engineer who can identify and fit the exact part' is disproportionate when a pointer to Sharp spares or a universal coupler with measurements would have finished the job.
